name: Hammedata (Haman's father)
title: Ancestor of the Agagites
summary: Hammedata was the father of Haman, the powerful Persian official who sought to exterminate the Jewish people. As an Agagite, he was likely a descendant of the Amalekite royal house, which explains the deep hostility between his family and the Israelites.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Haman's father
keyEvents.description: Hammedata is identified as the father of Haman the Agagite when Haman is introduced in the book of Esther as a high-ranking official under King Ahasverus.

keyEvents.title: Agagite lineage
keyEvents.description: The term 'Agagite' links Hammedata and his family to the royal house of the Amalekites, who were Israel's ancient enemies from the time of the wilderness wanderings.

keyEvents.title: The family in a royal decree
keyEvents.description: Hammedata's name is mentioned in the royal decree that gave the Jews the right to defend themselves, serving as an identification of the enemy Haman.
